# Beat The Scam

> Plain-English UK consumer-protection guides covering scams, fraud, and how to spot them before paying. New guide published daily by an editorial team focused on UK consumers.

## Guides

### Crypto Scams

- [Binance Impersonation Scam UK: How to Spot Fake Messages and Protect Your Crypto](https://beatthescam.com/guides/binance-impersonation-scam-uk/): Criminals send fake Binance emails, SMS messages and social media messages claiming urgent action is needed on your account. They trick you into clicking malicious links or revealing your password, then drain your crypto wallet.
- [Bitcoin ATM Scam UK: How Criminals Trick You at Cash Machines](https://beatthescam.com/guides/bitcoin-atm-scam-uk/): Bitcoin ATM scams target UK residents by impersonating banks, tax authorities, or tech support, pressuring victims to withdraw cash and convert it to Bitcoin at ATMs. The money is irreversible and the scammers disappear once the transaction is complete.
- [Bitcoin Scam UK: How to Spot and Avoid Crypto Fraud](https://beatthescam.com/guides/bitcoin-scam-uk/): Bitcoin scams in the UK typically involve fraudsters posing as legitimate crypto platforms, investment advisors, or recovery services to steal money or personal data. This guide explains the most common Bitcoin scam patterns and how to protect yourself.
- [Crypto Recovery Scam UK: How Fraudsters Pose as Recovery Experts](https://beatthescam.com/guides/crypto-recovery-scam-uk/): Crypto recovery scams target people who have already lost money in investment fraud or hacking. Scammers impersonate recovery companies and charge upfront fees while stealing more funds or personal data.
- [Crypto Scams UK: How to Spot and Avoid Investment Fraud](https://beatthescam.com/guides/crypto-investment-scams-uk-protection/): Crypto scams cost UK residents millions every year. Scammers use fake investment platforms, celebrity endorsements, and pressure tactics to steal your money and personal data. This guide shows you exactly how these scams work and what to do if you've been targeted.
- [Cryptocurrency Payment Scam UK: How to Spot and Avoid Fake Crypto Exchanges](https://beatthescam.com/guides/cryptocurrency-payment-scam-uk/): Scammers impersonate legitimate cryptocurrency exchanges to trick UK users into sending money or cryptocurrency that cannot be recovered. This guide explains the exact tactics used, how to verify genuine platforms, and what to do if you've been targeted.
- [Fake Crypto Exchange UK: How to Spot and Avoid Scams](https://beatthescam.com/guides/fake-crypto-exchange-uk/): Fake crypto exchanges are designed to look identical to legitimate platforms like Coinbase or Kraken, but they steal your login details and funds. This guide shows you the specific warning signs and verification steps UK residents need to know.
- [NFT Scam UK: How to Spot Fake NFT Platforms and Protect Your Money](https://beatthescam.com/guides/nft-scam-uk/): NFT scams in the UK use fake websites and social media to lure investors into buying worthless digital assets or stealing login credentials. We explain how these scams work and the specific warning signs to watch for.

### Email Scams

- [Amazon Scam Emails: How to Spot a Fake Amazon Email (UK)](https://beatthescam.com/guides/amazon-order-scam-email-checklist/): Got an Amazon email about an order problem, refund, or 'account locked'? How to tell a genuine Amazon email from a phishing scam — and check safely.
- [CEO Fraud Email Scam UK: How to Spot and Stop Impersonation Attacks](https://beatthescam.com/guides/ceo-fraud-email-scam-uk/): CEO fraud, also called business email compromise (BEC), is a targeted scam where criminals impersonate company executives to trick employees into transferring funds or revealing sensitive information. This guide shows you the exact warning signs and verification steps UK businesses and employees need to know.
- [Companies House Email Scam UK: How to Spot and Avoid Fake Official Emails](https://beatthescam.com/guides/companies-house-email-scam-uk/): Fraudsters send emails pretending to be from Companies House, the UK government agency that registers companies. They demand urgent payment for filing fees, renewals, or threaten to strike your company off the register unless you act immediately.
- [DVLA Email Scam UK: How to Spot and Avoid Fake DVLA Emails](https://beatthescam.com/guides/dvla-email-scam-uk/): Fraudsters send fake DVLA emails claiming you owe vehicle tax, need to update your license, or have a traffic violation. These emails trick you into clicking malicious links or revealing sensitive information like your driving license number and bank details.
- [Email Account Takeover Scam UK: How to Spot and Stop It](https://beatthescam.com/guides/email-account-takeover-scam-uk/): Email account takeover is when criminals break into your email account to steal money, personal data, or impersonate you to others. This guide explains how the scam works, what warning signs to watch for, and exactly what to do if you think your account has been compromised.
- [Festival Lineup Email Scam UK: How to Spot Fake Ticket Offers](https://beatthescam.com/guides/festival-lineup-email-scam-uk/): Festival lineup email scams trick UK music fans into clicking malicious links or paying for fake presale tickets. Scammers impersonate real festivals like Glastonbury, Reading, Leeds, and Latitude to harvest payment details and personal information.
- [HMRC Tax Rebate Email Scam: How to Spot and Avoid It in the UK](https://beatthescam.com/guides/hmrc-tax-rebate-email-scam/): HMRC tax rebate scams use convincing fake emails claiming you're owed a refund to steal your personal and financial data. This guide shows you exactly how to spot these emails and what to do if you've already clicked a link.
- [HSBC Phishing Email Scam UK: How to Spot and Stop It](https://beatthescam.com/guides/hsbc-phishing-email-scam-uk/): HSBC phishing emails trick customers into revealing login details, card numbers, or personal information by impersonating the bank. Scammers use urgent language, fake security alerts, and fraudulent links to steal credentials and access accounts.
- [Invoice Redirection Scam: UK Guide to Spotting Fake Payment Requests](https://beatthescam.com/guides/invoice-redirection-scam-checklist/): Invoice redirection scams intercept legitimate business communications and redirect payment to fraudster bank accounts. This guide shows you how to spot fake invoices, verify genuine requests, and protect your business payments.
- [Microsoft Account Suspended Email Scam: UK Guide to Spotting Fake Messages](https://beatthescam.com/guides/microsoft-account-suspended-email-scam-uk/): Scammers send convincing emails claiming your Microsoft account has been suspended and asking you to verify your identity urgently. These emails lead to fake login pages designed to steal your password, recovery email, and payment card details.
- [NatWest Phishing Email Scam: UK Guide to Spotting Fake Messages](https://beatthescam.com/guides/natwest-phishing-email-uk/): NatWest phishing emails trick customers into revealing login details and personal information by pretending to be urgent account alerts. This guide shows you how to identify fake NatWest emails and what to do if you've been targeted.
- [Netflix Billing Email Scam UK: How to Spot Fake Payment Notices](https://beatthescam.com/guides/netflix-billing-email-scam-uk/): Netflix billing email scams target UK subscribers by sending urgent messages claiming payment has failed or your account needs updating. Victims are directed to fake login pages where their email, password, and payment information are stolen.
- [PayPal Account Limited Email Scam UK: How to Spot and Avoid It](https://beatthescam.com/guides/paypal-account-limited-email-scam-uk/): Scammers send fake PayPal emails claiming your account is limited, asking you to verify your identity or payment details. We show you how to spot the fake emails and stay safe.
- [Santander Email Scam: How to Spot a Fake Bank Email (UK)](https://beatthescam.com/guides/santander-email-scam-uk/): A Santander email about a locked account or 'verify now'? How to spot a fake Santander email, check it safely, and report phishing in the UK.
- [Sextortion Email Scam UK: How to Spot and Stop It](https://beatthescam.com/guides/sextortion-email-scam-uk/): Sextortion is a blackmail scam delivered by email, where criminals claim to have intimate footage or screenshots and demand payment to keep quiet. These emails are almost always false, but they exploit fear and shame to pressure victims into paying.
- [TV Licence Email Scam UK: How to Spot Fake TV Licensing Demands](https://beatthescam.com/guides/tv-licence-email-scam-uk/): TV licence email scams use official-looking messages claiming you owe a fine or renewal payment to steal money or identity information. Scammers create fake websites and demand urgent payment before your account is suspended or enforcement action is taken.

### Employment Scams

- [Data Entry Job Scam UK: How to Spot Fake Work-from-Home Offers](https://beatthescam.com/guides/data-entry-job-scam-uk/): Data entry job scams target UK job seekers with promises of quick, flexible work from home. Fraudsters collect upfront fees for training, software, or equipment, or steal personal information to commit identity fraud.
- [Indeed Job Scams UK: How to Spot a Fake Recruiter](https://beatthescam.com/guides/indeed-job-scam-uk/): A great-paying Indeed job that asks for an upfront fee or moves you to WhatsApp? How to spot a fake recruiter — and why a real UK employer never charges you to work.
- [Job Offer Scam: How to Spot Fake Recruitment in the UK](https://beatthescam.com/guides/job-offer-scam-uk/): Job offer scams trick people into sending money or sharing sensitive information by pretending to be legitimate employers or recruitment agencies. Scammers often target job seekers on LinkedIn, Indeed, and via email, offering unusually high pay with minimal qualifications required.
- [LinkedIn Job Scam: How to Spot Fake Recruitment Offers in the UK](https://beatthescam.com/guides/linkedin-job-scam-guide-uk/): Scammers create convincing LinkedIn profiles posing as recruiters or hiring managers, offering fake jobs to lure UK job seekers. They often ask for upfront fees, bank details, or personal information under the pretence of processing applications or background checks.
- [Mystery Shopper Scam UK: How to Spot Fake Jobs and Protect Yourself](https://beatthescam.com/guides/mystery-shopper-scam-uk/): Mystery shopper scams target job seekers with promises of easy money for shopping and reviewing. Scammers pose as legitimate mystery shopping companies, but ask you to pay upfront fees or complete suspicious tasks that result in financial loss.
- [Recruitment Agency Scam UK: How to Spot Fake Job Offers and Protect Yourself](https://beatthescam.com/guides/recruitment-agency-scam-uk/): Recruitment agency scams target vulnerable job seekers in the UK by impersonating legitimate employment agencies or creating fake job listings. Scammers typically request upfront fees, personal data, or bank details under the pretence of processing applications or conducting background checks.
- [Remote Work Scam UK 2026: How to Spot Fake Job Offers and Protect Yourself](https://beatthescam.com/guides/remote-work-scam-uk-2026/): Remote work scams have surged in 2026, with fraudsters posing as legitimate employers to steal money and identity information from UK job seekers. This guide explains how these scams work and gives you practical steps to verify job offers and stay safe.
- [Work from Home Scam UK: How to Spot and Avoid Fake Job Offers](https://beatthescam.com/guides/work-from-home-scam-uk/): Work from home scams target UK job seekers with promises of quick money for minimal effort, often using fake job boards and impersonated companies. This guide shows you exactly how these scams operate and what steps to take if you've been contacted.

### Fraud & Impersonation

- [beatthescam.com Guide: Spotting and Avoiding UK Consumer Scams](https://beatthescam.com/guides/beatthescamcom-guide-spotting-and-avoiding-uk-consumer-scams/): Complete guide to identifying common UK scams and protecting yourself. Learn warning signs, reporting procedures, and defence strategies from verified consumer threats.
- [Charity Scams UK: How to Spot Fake Charities and Protect Your Donation](https://beatthescam.com/guides/charity-donation-scam-checklist/): Charity scams impersonate real charities or create fake ones to trick donors into sending money that never reaches those in need. Scammers use emotional appeals, fake websites, and convincing emails to steal donations—sometimes thousands of pounds.
- [Conveyancing Fraud UK: How to Spot and Stop Property Purchase Scams](https://beatthescam.com/guides/conveyancing-fraud-uk/): Conveyancing fraud is a sophisticated crime where criminals impersonate your solicitor or conveyancer to intercept property funds. This guide explains how the scam works, what warning signs to watch for, and how to protect yourself during a property transaction.
- [Deed Fraud UK Property Scam: How to Protect Your Home](https://beatthescam.com/guides/deed-fraud-uk-property-scam/): Deed fraud involves criminals forging documents to claim ownership of your property or use it as security for loans without your knowledge. This guide explains how the scam works, what to watch for, and the urgent steps to take if you suspect your property has been targeted.
- [Driveway Cowboy Scam UK: How to Spot Fake Contractors](https://beatthescam.com/guides/driveway-cowboy-scam-uk/): Driveway cowboy scams target UK homeowners with unsolicited offers to repair or resurface driveways at suspiciously low prices. These fraudsters collect upfront deposits and vanish without completing work, or use fake company names and identities to avoid being traced.
- [Google Voice Verification Code Scam UK: Don't Share That Code](https://beatthescam.com/guides/google-voice-verification-scam/): Someone asks you to read back a Google verification code to 'prove you're real'? It's a scam to hijack your number. Here's how it works and what to do.
- [Identity Theft UK: How to Spot and Stop It Before Your Details Are Used](https://beatthescam.com/guides/identity-theft-uk/): Identity theft in the UK involves criminals stealing your personal information—name, address, National Insurance number, or bank details—to commit fraud in your name. We explain the warning signs, how the scam works, and exactly what to do if you think you're a victim.
- [Impersonation Scams: When Criminals Pretend to Be Your Bank or the Police](https://beatthescam.com/guides/impersonation-scams-when-criminals-pretend-to-be-your-bank-or-the-police/): Learn how impersonation scams work in the UK, recognise the warning signs, and protect yourself from criminals posing as trusted organisations. This guide helps consumers avoid losing money to fake calls and messages.
- [Mandate Fraud UK: How Scammers Steal Direct Debit Access](https://beatthescam.com/guides/mandate-fraud-uk-businesses/): Mandate fraud is when criminals impersonate your supplier or service provider and convince you to alter your direct debit instructions. The scammer redirects your regular payments to their own bank account, potentially costing thousands before you notice.
- [Recovery Scam UK: How Scammers Pose as Refund Services](https://beatthescam.com/guides/refund-recovery-scam-warning-signs/): Recovery scams target people who have already lost money to fraud, promising to retrieve their funds for an upfront fee. Scammers impersonate legitimate refund companies, lawyers, or financial investigators to gain trust and extract payment.
- [WhatsApp 'New Number' Scam UK: How to Spot Family Impersonation Tricks](https://beatthescam.com/guides/whatsapp-family-emergency-scam/): Scammers access or create WhatsApp accounts and message your contacts pretending to be a family member with a new phone number. They quickly build trust before asking for urgent financial help, often citing emergencies like hospital bills or legal problems.

### Government Impersonation

- [Benefits Fraud Text Scam UK: How to Spot and Avoid DWP Impersonation](https://beatthescam.com/guides/benefits-fraud-text-scam-uk/): Criminals send fake text messages claiming to be from the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP), asking you to verify your identity, confirm bank details, or click a link. These messages are designed to harvest your personal information or trick you into paying fake fines or fees.
- [Companies House Scam Letter UK: How to Spot and Report It](https://beatthescam.com/guides/companies-house-scam-letter-uk/): Scammers send official-looking letters claiming to be from Companies House, often demanding urgent payment for company registration or compliance fees. This guide explains how to spot these letters, verify genuine communications, and report them to the authorities.
- [Council Housing Scam UK: How to Spot and Avoid Fake Housing Offers](https://beatthescam.com/guides/council-housing-scam-uk/): Council housing scams target people desperate for affordable accommodation by posing as local authority housing departments. Scammers demand upfront fees, deposits, or personal information, then disappear or use stolen data for identity fraud.
- [Court Summons Scam Email UK: How to Spot Fake HMCTS Messages](https://beatthescam.com/guides/court-summons-scam-email-uk/): Fraudsters send official-looking emails claiming you have an unpaid fine or court appearance, pressuring you to click links or pay immediately. This guide shows you how to verify genuine HMCTS contact and what to do if you've already responded.
- [DVLA Email Scam Car Tax: How to Spot Fake Renewal Emails in the UK](https://beatthescam.com/guides/dvla-email-scam-car-tax/): Scammers send convincing fake DVLA emails claiming your car tax is expiring or needs urgent renewal, complete with official-looking logos and buttons. They trick you into paying for non-existent tax or stealing your personal data and bank details.
- [HMRC Self Assessment Scam UK: How to Spot and Avoid It](https://beatthescam.com/guides/hmrc-self-assessment-scam-uk/): Scammers send emails, texts, and letters pretending to be HMRC, claiming you owe tax or must verify your self-assessment details urgently. This guide explains how the scam works, what genuine HMRC contact looks like, and what to do if you've already engaged with a fake message.
- [Passport Renewal Scam UK: How to Spot Fake HMPO Requests](https://beatthescam.com/guides/passport-renewal-scam-uk/): Scammers impersonate the UK Passport Office (HMPO) to trick people into paying fake fees or handing over personal data. This guide shows you how to spot these scams, verify genuine requests, and what to do if you've already been contacted.
- [Student Finance Scam UK: How to Spot and Avoid Fake Loan Offers](https://beatthescam.com/guides/student-finance-scam-uk/): Student Finance scams target UK students with fake loan offers, fake repayment demands, and phishing emails that look like official government communications. Scammers use urgency and authority to trick you into sharing bank details, passwords, or paying upfront fees.
- [TV Licence Scam Letter UK: How to Spot Fake Demands and Protect Yourself](https://beatthescam.com/guides/tv-licence-scam-letter-uk/): TV Licensing scam letters trick householders into paying fake fines or providing personal details by impersonating the official BBC-owned TV Licensing authority. We show you exactly how to tell the difference between genuine letters and scam copies, and what to do if you've already engaged with one.
- [UKVI Visa Scam UK: How to Spot Fake Home Office Immigration Emails](https://beatthescam.com/guides/ukvi-visa-scam-uk/): Criminals send fake emails claiming to be from UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI), the Home Office immigration service. They demand urgent payment for visa applications, extensions, or claims of overpayment refunds—then disappear with your money and identity details.
- [Universal Credit Scam UK: How to Spot and Avoid DWP Impersonation Fraud](https://beatthescam.com/guides/universal-credit-scam-uk/): Universal Credit scams involve fraudsters pretending to be the Department of Work and Pensions, usually via text, email, or phone calls. They create false urgency about account suspensions or overpayments to trick you into revealing bank details, passwords, or sending money.

### Investment & Finance Scams

- [Bond Scam UK: How Fraudsters Steal via Fake Investments](https://beatthescam.com/guides/bond-scam-uk/): Bond scams promise unusually high returns on investment bonds, then ask for upfront fees or deposits that disappear. Fraudsters often impersonate legitimate investment firms or create convincing fake websites to steal thousands from unsuspecting UK residents.
- [Clone Firm Investment Scam UK: How to Spot Fake FCA-Regulated Companies](https://beatthescam.com/guides/clone-firm-investment-scam-uk/): Clone firm scams target UK savers by impersonating legitimate, FCA-regulated investment companies. Fraudsters create near-identical websites and contact details to convince you to invest money that disappears immediately.
- [Debt Management Scam UK: How to Spot Fake Debt Relief Companies](https://beatthescam.com/guides/debt-management-scam-uk/): Debt management scams target people with existing debts by impersonating regulated firms and demanding upfront fees for services that never materialise. Scammers often use pressure tactics and false promises to negotiate your debts, then disappear with your money.
- [Debt Relief Scam UK: How to Spot and Avoid Fake Debt Help](https://beatthescam.com/guides/debt-relief-scam-uk/): Scammers pose as debt advisers or consolidation companies, promising to reduce or erase your debts in exchange for upfront fees. They target people in financial difficulty and often use pressure tactics and fake credentials to gain trust.
- [Fake Trading Platform Scams UK: How to Spot Fraudulent Investment Sites](https://beatthescam.com/guides/fake-trading-platform-uk/): Fake trading platforms are websites designed to look like real investment brokers, where scammers trick you into depositing money or handing over sensitive financial information. These sites often target UK investors with promises of high returns on forex, cryptocurrency, or stocks.
- [Forex Trading Scam UK: How to Spot Fake Trading Platforms & Protect Your Money](https://beatthescam.com/guides/forex-trading-scam-uk/): Forex trading scams target UK residents with promises of easy profits from currency trading. Scammers use fake regulated brokers, high-pressure sales tactics, and manipulation of trading software to steal deposits and personal data.
- [IVA Scam UK: How to Spot and Avoid Individual Voluntary Arrangement Fraud](https://beatthescam.com/guides/iva-scam-uk/): IVA (Individual Voluntary Arrangement) scams target people struggling with debt by impersonating legitimate debt advisers. Scammers collect upfront fees or personal information under false pretences, leaving victims worse off financially.
- [Land Banking Scam UK: How to Spot and Avoid Property Investment Fraud](https://beatthescam.com/guides/land-banking-scam-uk/): Land banking scams target property investors by selling worthless or non-existent UK land plots at inflated prices, promising rapid appreciation. Scammers use high-pressure sales tactics, fake documentation, and promises of guaranteed returns to persuade victims to part with tens of thousands of pounds.
- [Money Mule Scam UK: How to Spot and Avoid Being Recruited](https://beatthescam.com/guides/money-mule-scam-uk/): Money mule scams lure UK residents into moving stolen money through their bank accounts in exchange for a cut of the proceeds. If you fall for this, you could face criminal charges even if you didn't know the money was stolen.
- [Pension Cold Call Scam UK: How to Spot and Stop This Scam](https://beatthescam.com/guides/pension-cold-call-scam-uk/): Pension cold call scams target people by pretending to be legitimate financial advisers offering pension reviews or early access schemes. The scammers convince you to transfer your pension pot into fraudulent accounts, leaving your retirement savings gone forever.
- [Ponzi Scheme UK Warning: How to Spot Investment Scams](https://beatthescam.com/guides/ponzi-scheme-uk-warning/): Ponzi schemes are illegal investment frauds that collapse when new investor money runs out. In the UK, scammers often pose as legitimate investment firms, using social media and WhatsApp to recruit victims and promise guaranteed high returns.
- [Recovery Room Scam UK: How to Spot and Avoid Fake Debt Recovery Schemes](https://beatthescam.com/guides/recovery-room-scam-uk/): Recovery room scams promise to retrieve money lost to previous fraud, but are themselves sophisticated fraud schemes. Scammers pose as debt recovery firms, lawyers, or financial investigators to extract upfront fees and personal data from desperate victims.
- [Share Fraud UK: How to Spot and Avoid Investment Scams](https://beatthescam.com/guides/share-fraud-uk/): Share fraud is a growing threat where scammers pose as legitimate investment brokers or advisors to convince you to buy fake shares or invest in non-existent companies. This guide explains how the scam works, what to watch for, and what steps to take if you've been contacted.

### Marketplace Scams

- [Airbnb Scam UK Listings: How to Spot Fake Properties and Protect Yourself](https://beatthescam.com/guides/airbnb-scam-uk-listings/): Fraudsters create fake Airbnb listings or hijack real accounts to steal deposits, collect advance payments for properties that don't exist, or harvest personal information. This guide shows you exactly what to watch for and how to verify genuine UK Airbnb properties before you book.
- [AutoTrader Car Scam UK: How to Spot Fake Listings and Protect Yourself](https://beatthescam.com/guides/autotrader-car-scam-uk/): AutoTrader scams typically involve fake car listings created by criminals impersonating genuine sellers or using stolen seller accounts. Victims are persuaded to pay deposits or full purchase prices for vehicles that don't exist or aren't for sale.
- [Depop Scam UK: How to Spot and Avoid Fake Sellers and Payment Fraud](https://beatthescam.com/guides/depop-scam-uk/): Depop is a popular UK fashion resale app, but scammers exploit it heavily. This guide covers the main scam patterns affecting UK users: fake seller accounts, off-platform payment demands, counterfeit item sales, and account takeovers.
- [eBay Listing Fee Scam UK: How to Spot and Avoid It](https://beatthescam.com/guides/ebay-listing-fee-scam-uk/): The eBay listing fee scam targets UK sellers with fake payment requests for listing fees, often sent via email or text. Scammers create urgency by claiming your account will be suspended unless you pay immediately.
- [eBay Scams UK: How to Spot a Fake Buyer, Seller or Email](https://beatthescam.com/guides/ebay-buyer-scam-uk/): Asked to pay or deal outside eBay, or got an 'eBay' email about a held payment? How to spot the common eBay scams and keep your money protected.
- [Etsy Scam Sellers UK Guide: How to Spot Fake Shops and Avoid Losing Money](https://beatthescam.com/guides/etsy-scam-sellers-uk-guide/): Etsy attracts both genuine craftspeople and scammers posing as legitimate sellers. This guide explains common Etsy seller scams, red flags to spot before payment, and exactly what to do if you've been targeted.
- [Facebook Marketplace Fake Buyer Scam UK: How to Spot and Avoid It](https://beatthescam.com/guides/facebook-marketplace-fake-buyer-scam-uk/): Facebook Marketplace fake buyer scams target UK sellers by impersonating legitimate buyers, then either disappearing after payment or using fake payment confirmations to claim items without paying. This guide shows you exactly how these scams work and how to protect yourself.
- [Facebook Marketplace Scam UK: How to Spot Fake Sellers and Protect Your Money](https://beatthescam.com/guides/facebook-marketplace-scam-uk/): Facebook Marketplace scams cost UK buyers thousands every year through fake listings, fake payment systems, and non-delivery of goods. This guide shows you exactly how to verify sellers, spot red flags before you pay, and what to do if you've already sent money.
- [Festival Camping Equipment Vinted Scam: UK Guide to Spotting Fake Sellers](https://beatthescam.com/guides/festival-camping-equipment-vinted-scam/): Festival season brings a surge of fake camping equipment listings on Vinted, where scammers use stolen photos and pressure tactics to trick buyers into paying outside the app. This guide explains how the scam works and exactly what to check before buying.
- [Gumtree Scams UK: How to Spot and Avoid Fake Listings and Buyers](https://beatthescam.com/guides/gumtree-scam-uk-guide/): Gumtree is legitimate, but scammers use it. Here are the most common Gumtree scams targeting UK buyers and sellers, the warning signs, and how to stay safe.
- [Preloved Scam UK: How to Spot Fake Sellers and Protect Yourself](https://beatthescam.com/guides/preloved-scam-uk/): Preloved is a popular UK marketplace for second-hand goods, but scammers exploit it to trick buyers into paying for items that don't exist or transferring money outside the platform. This guide shows you exactly how these scams work and what steps to take to protect yourself.
- [Rightmove Rental Scam UK: How to Spot Fake Properties and Protect Yourself](https://beatthescam.com/guides/rightmove-rental-scam-uk/): Rightmove rental scams target renters searching for properties by impersonating legitimate landlords or agents. Scammers create fake listings or clone existing ones, then request deposits before you've viewed the property or signed a contract.
- [Shpock scam UK: how to spot and avoid fake sellers on the app](https://beatthescam.com/guides/shpock-scam-uk/): Shpock is a legitimate UK secondhand marketplace app, but scammers actively impersonate genuine sellers or create fake listings to defraud users. This guide shows you exactly how the scam works and what to check before you buy or sell anything.
- [Vinted Buyer Scam UK: How to Spot and Avoid Fake Purchase Schemes](https://beatthescam.com/guides/vinted-buyer-scam-uk/): Vinted buyer scams target UK sellers by impersonating legitimate buyers or creating fake payment schemes. Scammers either disappear after claiming payment or trick sellers into sending money for 'verification' before the sale completes.
- [Vinted scams UK: how to spot and avoid fake sellers and buyers](https://beatthescam.com/guides/vinted-scam-warning-uk/): Vinted is a legitimate peer-to-peer marketplace, but scammers use fake seller and buyer accounts to steal money, personal details, or goods. - [Overpayment Scam UK: How to Spot and Avoid This Common Fraud](https://beatthescam.com/guides/overpayment-scam-uk/): Overpayment scams trick you into sending money back after receiving a payment that appears legitimate but is actually fraudulent. - [PayPal Friends and Family Scam UK: How to Spot and Avoid It](https://beatthescam.com/guides/paypal-friends-family-scam-uk/): The PayPal Friends and Family scam tricks UK users into sending money to criminals by posing as sellers, buyers, or trusted contacts. Unlike standard PayPal transactions, Friends and Family payments offer no protection — once sent, the money is nearly impossible to recover.
- [Push Payment Fraud UK: How Scammers Trick You Into Sending Your Own Money](https://beatthescam.com/guides/push-payment-fraud-uk/): Push payment fraud is when a scammer impersonates your bank, a business, or a trusted contact to convince you to send money directly from your account. - [Wedding Photographer Scam UK: How to Spot Fake Bookings & Protect Your Money](https://beatthescam.com/guides/wedding-photographer-scam-uk/): Wedding photographer scams involve fraudsters impersonating real professionals or creating fake portfolios to collect deposits for non-existent services. ### Phone Scams

- [Amazon Scam Phone Calls UK: How to Spot a Fake Amazon Call](https://beatthescam.com/guides/amazon-phone-call-scam-uk/): Got an automated 'Amazon' call about a suspicious order or account? It's almost certainly a scam. Here's how the fake Amazon call works and how to stop it.

UK banks will never call you asking for passwords, PINs, or verification codes—knowing this key fact could save you thousands of pounds.
- [BT Scam Calls: How to Spot a Fake BT Phone Call (UK)](https://beatthescam.com/guides/bt-broadband-scam-calls-uk/): An unexpected 'BT' call about your router, a refund, or being cut off? How to spot a fake BT caller, and what a genuine BT call will never ask.

- [HMRC Phone Call Scam UK: How to Spot and Stop Tax Fraud Calls](https://beatthescam.com/guides/hmrc-phone-call-scam-uk/): HMRC phone call scams trick UK residents into revealing personal details or paying fake tax bills by impersonating tax officials. - [HSBC Bank Scam Call UK: How to Spot and Stop Phone Impersonators](https://beatthescam.com/guides/hsbc-bank-scam-call-uk/): Scammers call pretending to be HSBC fraud teams, claiming suspicious activity on your account and asking you to verify details or download apps. - [National Insurance Scam Call UK: HMRC Impersonation Guide](https://beatthescam.com/guides/national-insurance-scam-call-uk/): Scammers ring claiming to be HMRC, threatening arrest or benefit suspension over fake National Insurance issues. These calls are never genuine—HMRC contacts you by post, not unexpected phone calls.
- [Number Spoofing Scam UK: How to Spot Fake Caller ID and Stay Safe](https://beatthescam.com/guides/number-spoofing-scam-uk/): Number spoofing is when criminals use technology to make their phone number appear as something trusted — like your bank or the HMRC — so you answer and engage with them. UK residents lose millions yearly to spoofed calls because the fake caller ID makes the scam seem legitimate.
- [Pension Liberation Scam UK: How to Spot and Stop Cold Calls](https://beatthescam.com/guides/pension-liberation-scam-uk/): Pension liberation scams target UK savers with promises of accessing their pension before age 55. - [Sky Broadband Scam Calls UK: How to Spot and Stop Them](https://beatthescam.com/guides/sky-broadband-scam-call-uk/): Sky broadband scam calls are one of the most common phone fraud attempts in the UK, with fraudsters pretending to be Sky customer service representatives. - [Yodel Scam Text Messages: How to Spot a Fake Yodel Text (UK)](https://beatthescam.com/guides/yodel-scam-text-messages/): Fake Yodel texts about a missed parcel or small 'redelivery' fee are smishing scams. Here's how to spot a fake Yodel text, check a real one, and report it in the UK.

### Travel Scams

- [Airport Transfer Taxi Scam UK: How to Spot and Avoid Fake Minicabs](https://beatthescam.com/guides/airport-transfer-taxi-scam-uk/): Airport transfer taxi scams target UK travellers at their most vulnerable—arriving tired and wanting quick transport. Scammers create fake websites, send phishing emails posing as airport services, or approach you in arrivals offering inflated fares.
- [Booking.com Scam UK: How to Spot Fake Booking Emails and Protect Your Holiday](https://beatthescam.com/guides/booking-com-scam-uk/): Booking.com scams typically arrive as fake confirmation emails or payment alerts that direct you to a fraudulent website or ask you to update your details urgently. Scammers use these to capture your card details, passport information, and login credentials.
- [Fake Airline Ticket Scam UK: How to Spot and Avoid Holiday Booking Fraud](https://beatthescam.com/guides/fake-airline-ticket-scam-uk/): Fake airline ticket scams target UK holiday makers with bargain flights that don't exist. Fraudsters impersonate real airlines or create convincing fake booking sites, then vanish once you've paid.
- [Glastonbury Accommodation Scam UK: How to Spot Fake Bookings](https://beatthescam.com/guides/glastonbury-accommodation-scam-uk/): Scammers create fake Glastonbury accommodation listings on social media, messaging apps, and ad sites to steal deposits from festival-goers. This guide shows you exactly how to verify genuine bookings and protect yourself before sending any money.
- [Holiday Compensation Scam UK: How to Spot Fake Claims Handlers](https://beatthescam.com/guides/holiday-compensation-scam-uk/): Holiday compensation scams target UK travellers who are legitimately owed money for cancelled trips, delays, or poor service. Fraudsters impersonate established claims management companies or create fake ones, demanding upfront fees before pursuing compensation.
- [Holiday Let Scam UK: How to Spot Fake Rental Listings and Protect Your Money](https://beatthescam.com/guides/holiday-let-scam-uk/): Holiday let scams target UK holidaymakers by posting fake rental properties on legitimate platforms or fraudulent websites. Scammers typically request upfront deposits or full payment via untraceable methods, then disappear or use stolen photos.
- [Jet2 Holiday Scam UK: How to Spot and Avoid Fake Booking Websites](https://beatthescam.com/guides/jet2-holiday-scam-uk/): Jet2 holiday scams target UK travellers through convincing fake websites, text messages, and emails offering unusually cheap flights and package deals. Scammers collect payment and passport details, then disappear—leaving victims without flights or refunds.
- [Package Holiday Scam UK: How to Spot Fake Travel Deals and Protect Yourself](https://beatthescam.com/guides/package-holiday-scam-uk/): Package holiday scams target UK travellers with too-good-to-be-true deals on flights, hotels, and complete holiday packages. Fraudsters impersonate legitimate travel agents, create fake websites, and use social media to lure victims into paying upfront for holidays that never exist.
- [TUI Booking Scam UK: How to Spot Fake Holiday Offers and Protect Yourself](https://beatthescam.com/guides/tui-booking-scam-uk/): TUI booking scams target UK holidaymakers with fake confirmation emails, texts, and websites that look identical to the real TUI platform. Scammers create urgency around payment, cancellation fees, or security issues to trick you into sending money or revealing personal details.
- [Visa Application Scam UK: How to Spot Fake Immigration Services](https://beatthescam.com/guides/visa-application-scam-uk/): Visa application scams target people applying for UK visas by impersonating official government services or legitimate visa consultants. Fraudsters create convincing websites and emails to collect application fees and steal identity documents, leaving victims without a visa and thousands of pounds out of pocket.

### Utility Scams

- [British Gas scam call UK: how to spot and stop it](https://beatthescam.com/guides/british-gas-scam-call-uk/): Scammers call UK residents claiming to be from British Gas, often saying there's an urgent billing issue or safety concern. These calls aim to trick you into revealing bank details, passwords, or access to your account.
- [Smart Meter Scam Call UK: How to Spot and Avoid Energy Company Impostors](https://beatthescam.com/guides/smart-meter-scam-call-uk/): Smart meter scam calls typically come from criminals pretending to be from your energy supplier, claiming you need an urgent meter upgrade or inspection. They use pressure tactics and fake caller ID spoofing to convince you to let them into your home or hand over bank details.
- [Solar Panel Scam UK: How to Spot and Avoid Dodgy Installers](https://beatthescam.com/guides/solar-panel-scam-uk/): Scammers pose as solar panel installers or government-backed schemes to trap UK homeowners into expensive contracts or stealing personal data. This guide reveals common tactics, warning signs, and how to verify genuinely legitimate solar offers.

- [AliExpress Scam UK: How to Spot Fake Sellers and Protect Yourself](https://beatthescam.com/guides/aliexpress-scam-or-legit-uk-guide/): AliExpress scams typically involve fake sellers offering items at suspiciously low prices, taking payment, and either sending counterfeit goods or nothing at all. UK buyers are particularly targeted because of higher purchasing power, and scammers exploit AliExpress's dispute resolution system to avoid refunds.
- [ASOS copycat scam UK: how to spot fake ASOS websites and protect yourself](https://beatthescam.com/guides/asos-copycat-scam-uk/): Fake ASOS websites look almost identical to the real retailer but are designed to steal your payment card details and personal information.
